query: Chosen by the Nose {Mr Grimsby holds three books under your nose, one after another, eyes closed. "Don't look. Smell. The right book smells right."|Mr Grimsby greets you with a book already held out at nose height. "Vanilla and rain," he says. "Trust me."|Mr Grimsby hands you a book by its smell before you've closed the door. He hasn't asked what you came in for. He never does.} {One smells of pipe smoke and the sea.|One smells of cut grass and arguments.|{season == "winter": One smells of woodsmoke, and the shop is freezing.|One smells, faintly, of you.}} Buy the one that smells right {You buy the one that smells of the sea. It's a book of storms, beautifully written and of no use whatsoever. You love it.|Vanilla and rain is a slim book of poems about lighthouses. Mr Grimsby wraps it like a gift and takes your coin as an afterthought.|You buy the one that smells like you. It's a novel about someone your age on the night before they leave home. You read it on the barge, slowly.} Insist on the one you came for {You describe the book four times. On the fifth, Mr Grimsby lights up and produces it from under a cat-sized stack. He seems a little disappointed in you.|You stand firm. Mr Grimsby sighs, sniffs the air and goes straight to the right shelf. He could do this all along.|You've learned to describe a book by its smell. Mr Grimsby finds yours in a minute, beaming at your progress.} {You ask for a textbook and leave, somehow, with nothing at all, after an hour's lecture on the smell of old maps.|Mr Grimsby goes into the shelves for your book and is gone so long you leave a note.|Mr Grimsby brings you a cookbook, with great confidence, and is so hurt when you decline it that you stay an hour to make up for it.}
